analyzed_vuln.description: `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` converts an ID-table entry from referring to a live attribute into a streaming-reader entry by assigning `id->name = attr->name` and clearing `id->attr`, but it does not duplicate or dictionary-intern the name. With `XML_PARSE_NODICT`, the attribute name is independently heap-allocated. `xmlTextReaderFreeProp` subsequently frees `cur->name`, leaving `id->name` dangling. At reader/document teardown, `xmlTextReaderFreeDoc` frees the ID table and `xmlFreeID` frees the dangling `id->name` again, causing the observed double-free. The fix belongs in `xmlTextReaderRemoveID`: transfer ownership safely or make an owned copy (while preserving dictionary semantics) before the attribute is reclaimed.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The harness consumes the first 4 bytes as parser options and the next 8 bytes as the encoding-string length; in this PoV they select options including `XML_PARSE_NODICT` and an empty encoding, leaving `` as file contents. Parsing must register an `xml:id` in `doc->ids`, then the streaming text reader must discard the element/attribute before document teardown. Because dictionary names are disabled, the `xml:id` attribute name is heap-owned; removal changes the ID entry to point at that name, attribute cleanup frees it, and `xmlFreeTextReader` later frees it again through the retained ID-table entry. Recovery-related options allow the malformed prefix/doctype portion of this PoV to reach that path.

args: Analyze the ownership semantics around xmlTextReaderRemoveID, xmlFreeID, and xmlTextReaderFreeProp in libxml2/xmlreader.c, especially with and without XML_PARSE_NODICT. What is the safest minimal root-cause fix, and are there existing analogous ownership-transfer patterns elsewhere in libxml2?

The provided ASan report shows a double-free in xmlFreeID at libxml2/xmlreader.c:249 after xmlTextReaderFreeProp previously frees the same attribute name. xmlTextReaderRemoveID currently appears to convert an ID entry from live attribute form by assigning id->name = attr->name and clearing id->attr. Under XML_PARSE_NODICT, attr->name is separately allocated, so later attribute reclamation invalidates id->name. The requested fix should preserve dictionary behavior and handle allocation failure correctly, while touching only C/C++ source under libxml2.

I applied the pattern from valid.c xmlAddID: if doc->dict then xmlDictLookup(doc->dict, attr->name, -1), else xmlStrdup; then id->attr=NULL and return -1 on NULL. test_patch still triggers dedup __interceptor_free--xmlFreeID--xmlHashFree.
